objects.description: Opaque decoder handle type for libmpg123. It encapsulates decoder state and is required by most API calls. Only forward-declared here; internal layout is hidden.

objects.description: Enumeration of parameter keys usable with mpg123_param/mpg123_getparam and their pars equivalents.
Bit flags used with MPG123_FLAGS family to control decoder behavior (mono/stereo forcing, resync, gapless, etc.).
Choices for ReplayGain/volume adjustment handling via MPG123_RVA parameter.
Feature keys for querying library capabilities via mpg123_feature().

objects.description: Error and message return codes used by libmpg123 APIs.

objects.definition:
enum mpg123_enc_enum
{
	 MPG123_ENC_8      = 0x00f
	,MPG123_ENC_16     = 0x040
	,MPG123_ENC_32     = 0x100
	,MPG123_ENC_SIGNED = 0x080
	,MPG123_ENC_FLOAT  = 0xe00
	,MPG123_ENC_SIGNED_16   = (MPG123_ENC_16|MPG123_ENC_SIGNED|0x10)
	,MPG123_ENC_UNSIGNED_16 = (MPG123_ENC_16|0x20)
	,MPG123_ENC_UNSIGNED_8  = 0x01
	,MPG123_ENC_SIGNED_8    = (MPG123_ENC_SIGNED|0x02)
	,MPG123_ENC_ULAW_8      = 0x04
	,MPG123_ENC_ALAW_8      = 0x08
	,MPG123_ENC_SIGNED_32   = MPG123_ENC_32|MPG123_ENC_SIGNED|0x1000
	,MPG123_ENC_UNSIGNED_32 = MPG123_ENC_32|0x2000
	,MPG123_ENC_FLOAT_32    = 0x200
	,MPG123_ENC_FLOAT_64    = 0x400
	,MPG123_ENC_ANY = ( MPG123_ENC_SIGNED_16  | MPG123_ENC_UNSIGNED_16 | MPG123_ENC_UNSIGNED_8 
	                  | MPG123_ENC_SIGNED_8   | MPG123_ENC_ULAW_8      | MPG123_ENC_ALAW_8
	                  | MPG123_ENC_SIGNED_32  | MPG123_ENC_UNSIGNED_32
	                  | MPG123_ENC_FLOAT_32   | MPG123_ENC_FLOAT_64 )
};
objects.description: Encoding bitflags and specific fully-qualified sample formats supported/recognized by mpg123.
Channel count indicators used in format negotiation.
Channel selector flags for EQ and volume APIs.
Variable bitrate mode enumeration for frame info.
MPEG version enumeration for frame info.
MPEG audio mode enumeration for frame info.
MPEG audio header flag bits for frame info.
Public structure filled by mpg123_info() to describe properties of the current MPEG frame/stream.
Keys for querying decoder/stream state (e.g., position accuracy) via mpg123_getstate().
Resizable string container used by metadata APIs; holds UTF-8 text and may contain multiple null-terminated substrings.
Internal normalized text encodings used for ID3/ICY conversion.
Raw ID3v2 encoding byte values; convertible via mpg123_enc_from_id3().
Container for an ID3v2 text frame (including comments/lyrics). Holds language, frame ID, description, and text as mpg123_string.
ID3v2 tag aggregate with pointers to last seen common fields and arrays for all encountered text/comment/extra frames. Strings are UTF-8.
Raw ID3v1/1.1 tag fields (fixed-size byte arrays).
Opaque parameter set object holding decoder configuration that can be applied to new handles; layout hidden.

functions.name: mpg123_init
functions.description: Initializes the libmpg123 library process-wide. Must be called exactly once before using any other libmpg123 API (including handle creation). Returns MPG123_OK on success or an error code.
requirements: Must be called exactly once per process before any other libmpg123 call.
Not thread-safe; do not call concurrently.

functions.name: mpg123_exit
functions.description: Shuts down the libmpg123 library process-wide. Call exactly once when finished using libmpg123.
requirements: Must be called exactly once per process, after mpg123_init().
Not thread-safe; do not call concurrently.
Should not be called while other libmpg123 calls are active.

functions.name: mpg123_new
functions.description: Creates a new decoder handle, optionally selecting a decoder by name and optionally returning an error code via the provided pointer.
requirements: mpg123_init() should have been called before creating handles.
decoder may be NULL for default decoder.
error may be NULL if caller does not want the error code.

functions.name: mpg123_delete
functions.description: Destroys a decoder handle and releases its resources. Safe to pass NULL.
requirements: mh must be a handle returned by mpg123_new()/mpg123_parnew(), or NULL.
Do not use mh after this call.

functions.name: mpg123_param
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_param(mpg123_handle *mh, enum mpg123_parms type, long value, double fvalue);
functions.description: Sets a decoder parameter on a handle using a key from mpg123_parms. Some keys use value (integer), some fvalue (float).
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
type must be one of mpg123_parms values.
Interpretation of value/fvalue depends on type (see enum comments).

functions.name: mpg123_getparam
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_getparam(mpg123_handle *mh, enum mpg123_parms type, long *val, double *fval);
functions.description: Retrieves a decoder parameter from a handle using a key from mpg123_parms into val/fval.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
type must be one of mpg123_parms values.
val and/or fval may be NULL if not needed; provide the appropriate one(s) for the queried type.

functions.name: mpg123_feature
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_feature(const enum mpg123_feature_set key);
functions.description: Queries whether a particular libmpg123 feature is available. Returns 1 if supported, 0 otherwise.
requirements: key must be one of mpg123_feature_set values.

functions.name: mpg123_plain_strerror
functions.description: Returns a constant human-readable string describing an error/message code.
requirements: errcode should be one of mpg123_errors values; other values may yield generic text.

functions.name: mpg123_strerror
functions.description: Returns a string for the last error that occurred in the context of the handle. If mh is NULL, returns message for MPG123_BAD_HANDLE.
requirements: mh may be NULL (handled).
Call after a function on mh returns MPG123_ERR to obtain reason.

functions.name: mpg123_errcode
functions.description: Returns the last error code stored in the handle instead of a string.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.

functions.name: mpg123_decoders
functions.description: Returns a NULL-terminated array of names of all available decoders (plain 8-bit ASCII).
requirements: Do not modify returned strings or array.
Array is NULL-terminated; iterate until NULL.

functions.name: mpg123_supported_decoders
functions.description: Returns a NULL-terminated array of decoder names supported by the current CPU.
requirements: Do not modify returned strings or array.
Array is NULL-terminated; iterate until NULL.

functions.name: mpg123_decoder
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_decoder(mpg123_handle *mh, const char* decoder_name);
functions.description: Selects the decoder engine by name for a handle.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
decoder_name must be a valid name from mpg123_decoders()/mpg123_supported_decoders().

functions.name: mpg123_current_decoder
functions.description: Returns the name of the currently active decoder engine for this handle, or NULL on error.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
Returned pointer must not be modified.

functions.name: mpg123_rates
functions.description: Provides the list of supported standard sample rates and its count.
requirements: list must be non-NULL to receive the pointer, or may be NULL if not needed.
number must be non-NULL to receive count, or may be NULL if not needed.
Do not modify the returned array.

functions.name: mpg123_encodings
functions.description: Provides the list of supported fully-qualified audio encodings and its count.
requirements: list must be non-NULL to receive the pointer, or may be NULL if not needed.
number must be non-NULL to receive count, or may be NULL if not needed.
Do not modify the returned array.

functions.name: mpg123_format_none
functions.description: Configures a handle to accept no output formats; use before enabling specific formats via mpg123_format().
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.

functions.name: mpg123_format_all
functions.description: Configures a handle to accept all output formats (default).
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.

functions.name: mpg123_format
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_format(mpg123_handle *mh, long rate, int channels, int encodings);
functions.description: Declares which output format(s) are acceptable on this handle for a given sample rate, channel configuration, and set of encodings.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
rate is a sample rate in Hz (can be non-standard when forcing).
channels is a combination of MPG123_STEREO and/or MPG123_MONO.
encodings is a bitwise combination of MPG123_ENC_* fully-qualified formats; unsupported ones are ignored.

functions.name: mpg123_format_support
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_format_support(mpg123_handle *mh, long rate, int encoding);
functions.description: Checks if a specific encoding at a given rate is supported; returns 0, MPG123_STEREO, MPG123_MONO, or their OR.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
encoding must be a fully-qualified MPG123_ENC_* value.
rate is in Hz.

functions.name: mpg123_getformat
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_getformat(mpg123_handle *mh, long *rate, int *channels, int *encoding);
functions.description: Retrieves the current output format (rate/channels/encoding) of the handle.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
Provide non-NULL pointers for desired outputs; any may be NULL if not needed.

functions.name: mpg123_open
functions.description: Opens a file by filesystem path and prepares the handle for decoding. Does not support HTTP URLs.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
path must be a valid filesystem path string.
For network streams, use mpg123_open_fd() or mpg123_open_feed() instead.

functions.name: mpg123_open_fd
functions.description: Prepares the handle to read from an already-open file descriptor as the bitstream source. mpg123_close() will not close the fd.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
fd must be an open, readable descriptor positioned at the start (or desired position) of an MPEG stream.
Caller retains responsibility to close fd.

functions.name: mpg123_open_feed
functions.description: Prepares the handle for direct input feeding via mpg123_feed()/mpg123_decode().
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
Caller must supply stream bytes via mpg123_feed or mpg123_decode.

functions.name: mpg123_close
functions.description: Closes the source if libmpg123 opened it via mpg123_open(). Does not close user-supplied file descriptors from mpg123_open_fd().
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.

functions.name: mpg123_read
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_read(mpg123_handle *mh, unsigned char *outmemory, size_t outmemsize, size_t *done);
functions.description: Reads from the stream and decodes up to outmemsize bytes into outmemory, storing the number of produced bytes in done. Returns error/message codes (e.g., MPG123_DONE, MPG123_NEW_FORMAT, MPG123_NEED_MORE).
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle with an open source (or in feed mode with data).
outmemory must be a valid writable buffer of at least outmemsize bytes (unless outmemsize is zero).
done must be a valid pointer to receive the produced byte count.

functions.name: mpg123_feed
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_feed(mpg123_handle *mh, const unsigned char *in, size_t size);
functions.description: Feeds input bytes to a handle opened with mpg123_open_feed(). Returns error/message codes.
requirements: mh must be opened with mpg123_open_feed().
in must point to size bytes of input; may be NULL only if size==0.

functions.name: mpg123_decode
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_decode(mpg123_handle *mh, const unsigned char *inmemory, size_t inmemsize, unsigned char *outmemory, size_t outmemsize, size_t *done);
functions.description: Parses/decodes MPEG Audio from input memory to output memory in one step. With zero-sized output buffer, only parses input to discover format changes (e.g., MPG123_NEW_FORMAT). Returns error/message codes (notably MPG123_NEED_MORE).
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle (feed or file mode).
If inmemsize>0, inmemory must be a valid pointer to input bytes; may be NULL if inmemsize==0.
outmemory must have at least outmemsize bytes if outmemsize>0; may be NULL if outmemsize==0 for parse-only.
done must be a valid pointer to receive produced byte count.

functions.name: mpg123_decode_frame
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_decode_frame(mpg123_handle *mh, off_t *num, unsigned char **audio, size_t *bytes);
functions.description: Decodes the next MPEG frame into an internal buffer or, if a new format is encountered, returns after setting the new format. Provides frame offset, pointer to internal audio buffer, and byte count.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle with an open source.
audio and bytes must be valid pointers to receive buffer pointer and size; audio points to internal memory (do not free/modify).
num may be NULL if caller does not need the frame offset.

functions.name: mpg123_framebyframe_decode
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_framebyframe_decode(mpg123_handle *mh, off_t *num, unsigned char **audio, size_t *bytes);
functions.description: Experimental API: decodes the current frame to the internal buffer (or reports format) in frame-by-frame mode. Subject to change.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle in appropriate state for frame-by-frame operations.
audio and bytes receive internal buffer pointer and size; do not modify/free.
num may be NULL if frame offset is not needed.

functions.name: mpg123_framebyframe_next
functions.description: Experimental API: finds, reads, and parses the next MP3 frame in frame-by-frame mode.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle prepared for frame-by-frame use.

functions.name: mpg123_tell
functions.description: Returns the current sample position (the next sample index to be returned by a read).
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle with an open source.

functions.name: mpg123_tellframe
functions.description: Returns the MPEG frame number that will be the source of the next decoded data.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle with an open source.

functions.name: mpg123_tell_stream
functions.description: Returns the current byte offset in the input stream.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle with an open source.

functions.name: mpg123_seek
functions.signature: EXPORT off_t mpg123_seek(mpg123_handle *mh, off_t sampleoff, int whence);
functions.description: Seeks to a desired sample offset relative to whence (SEEK_SET/SEEK_CUR/SEEK_END). Returns resulting offset or an error/message code.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle with a seekable source.
whence must be SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, or SEEK_END.
Sample-accurate seeking requires gapless support; otherwise frame-accurate.

functions.name: mpg123_feedseek
functions.signature: EXPORT off_t mpg123_feedseek(mpg123_handle *mh, off_t sampleoff, int whence, off_t *input_offset);
functions.description: Prepares a seek in feed mode: computes where to continue input feeding (input_offset) for the requested sample position. Returns resulting sample offset or error/message code.
requirements: mh must be opened with mpg123_open_feed().
input_offset must be a valid pointer to receive the expected next input byte position.
whence must be SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, or SEEK_END.

functions.name: mpg123_seek_frame
functions.signature: EXPORT off_t mpg123_seek_frame(mpg123_handle *mh, off_t frameoff, int whence);
functions.description: Seeks to a desired MPEG frame index relative to whence. Returns resulting frame index or an error/message code.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle with a seekable source.
whence must be SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, or SEEK_END.

functions.name: mpg123_timeframe
functions.description: Returns the MPEG frame index corresponding to the given time offset in seconds, assuming constant samples-per-frame within the stream.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
sec is a non-negative time offset for sensible results.

functions.name: mpg123_index
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_index(mpg123_handle *mh, off_t **offsets, off_t *step, size_t *fill);
functions.description: Provides access to the frame index table for seeking: returns pointer to index offsets array, step (frames per index entry), and number of filled entries.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle with index support.
offsets, step, and fill must be valid pointers to receive data; offsets points to internal data (do not modify/free).

functions.name: mpg123_set_index
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_set_index(mpg123_handle *mh, off_t *offsets, off_t step, size_t fill);
functions.description: Sets the frame index table. Passing offsets==NULL with fill>0 allocates fill entries; offsets==NULL and fill==0 clears and frees the index.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
If offsets is non-NULL, it must point to an array of at least fill entries.
step defines how many MPEG frames one index step represents.

functions.name: mpg123_position
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_position(mpg123_handle *mh, off_t frame_offset, off_t buffered_bytes, off_t *current_frame, off_t *frames_left, double *current_seconds, double *seconds_left);
functions.description: Returns projected current and remaining frame/second positions based on an offset from now and bytes already served but not yet played. Special-purpose API; may be removed.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
Provide non-NULL pointers for outputs you need; any may be NULL if not needed.
This does not account for gapless skipped samples.

functions.name: mpg123_eq
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_eq(mpg123_handle *mh, enum mpg123_channels channel, int band, double val);
functions.description: Sets a 32-band equalizer gain for the specified channel(s) and band index to a linear factor val.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
channel must be MPG123_LEFT, MPG123_RIGHT, or MPG123_LR.
band must be in the range 0..31.
val is a linear gain factor.

functions.name: mpg123_geteq
functions.signature: EXPORT double mpg123_geteq(mpg123_handle *mh, enum mpg123_channels channel, int band);
functions.description: Gets the 32-band equalizer setting (linear factor) for the specified channel(s) and band index.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
channel must be MPG123_LEFT, MPG123_RIGHT, or MPG123_LR (returns arithmetic mean for both).
band must be in the range 0..31.

functions.name: mpg123_reset_eq
functions.description: Resets the 32-band equalizer settings to flat for the handle.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.

functions.name: mpg123_volume
functions.description: Sets absolute output volume including RVA. If vol<0, only applies (possibly changed) RVA setting.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
vol is a linear amplitude factor; vol<0 means do not change base volume.

functions.name: mpg123_volume_change
functions.description: Adjusts output volume by the specified delta (linear factor) including RVA.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.

functions.name: mpg123_getvolume
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_getvolume(mpg123_handle *mh, double *base, double *really, double *rva_db);
functions.description: Returns current base volume, effective volume (including RVA), and RVA adjustment in dB.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
Provide non-NULL pointers for desired outputs; any may be NULL if not needed.

functions.name: mpg123_info
functions.description: Fills an mpg123_frameinfo structure with information about the current MPEG audio stream/frame.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle with an open source.
mi must be a valid pointer to writable struct mpg123_frameinfo.

functions.name: mpg123_safe_buffer
functions.description: Returns a safe output buffer size sufficient for all cases if replacing the internal buffer.
requirements: Use the returned size (or larger) for external output buffers to avoid overflow.

functions.name: mpg123_scan
functions.description: Performs a full parsing scan over the stream: finds ID3 tags, stores accurate length, fills the seek index, and seeks back to the current position. Refuses to work on non-seekable streams.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle with a seekable source.

functions.name: mpg123_length
functions.description: Returns the full expected length of the current track in samples if possible, or MPG123_ERR if not available.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
Meaningful only after sufficient stream information is known (e.g., after scan or when length is derivable).

functions.name: mpg123_set_filesize
functions.description: Overrides the file size in bytes (useful in feed mode or HTTP streams) to aid length estimation.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
size should be the total stream size in bytes.

functions.name: mpg123_tpf
functions.description: Returns the time (seconds) per MPEG frame for the current stream, or <0 on error.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.

functions.name: mpg123_clip
functions.description: Returns and resets the number of clipped samples since the last call.
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.

functions.name: mpg123_getstate
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_getstate(mpg123_handle *mh, enum mpg123_state key, long *val, double *fval);
functions.description: Retrieves current decoder/stream state information identified by key (e.g., MPG123_ACCURATE).
requirements: mh must be a valid mpg123_handle.
key must be a value from enum mpg123_state.
Provide non-NULL val/fval pointers appropriate for the key; unused output pointers may be NULL.

functions.name: mpg123_init_string
functions.description: Initializes a mpg123_string object and allocates its initial memory.
requirements: sb must be a valid pointer to mpg123_string.

functions.name: mpg123_free_string
functions.description: Frees memory held by a mpg123_string.
requirements: sb must be a valid pointer to mpg123_string (may represent an already-freed/empty string).
Do not use sb->p after freeing unless reinitialized.

functions.name: mpg123_resize_string
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_resize_string(mpg123_string* sb, size_t news);
functions.description: Resizes the mpg123_string buffer to exactly news bytes.
requirements: sb must be a valid pointer to mpg123_string.
news is the requested new buffer size in bytes.

functions.name: mpg123_grow_string
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_grow_string(mpg123_string* sb, size_t news);
functions.description: Ensures the mpg123_string buffer is at least news bytes, possibly keeping it larger.
requirements: sb must be a valid pointer to mpg123_string.
news is the minimum required size in bytes.

functions.name: mpg123_copy_string
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_copy_string(mpg123_string* from, mpg123_string* to);
functions.description: Copies the contents of one mpg123_string to another.
requirements: from and to must be valid pointers to mpg123_string.
to may be the same as from only if the implementation allows; safest to use distinct objects.

functions.name: mpg123_add_string
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_add_string(mpg123_string* sb, const char* stuff);
functions.description: Appends a C-string to an mpg123_string, ensuring null-termination.
requirements: sb must be a valid mpg123_string.
stuff must be a valid C-string (null-terminated).

functions.name: mpg123_add_substring
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_add_substring(mpg123_string *sb, const char *stuff, size_t from, size_t count);
functions.description: Appends a substring [from, from+count) from a C-string to an mpg123_string and appends a null byte.
requirements: sb must be a valid mpg123_string.
stuff must point to a valid character buffer with at least from+count bytes accessible.

functions.name: mpg123_set_string
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_set_string(mpg123_string* sb, const char* stuff);
functions.description: Replaces the contents of an mpg123_string with a C-string.
requirements: sb must be a valid mpg123_string.
stuff must be a valid C-string (null-terminated).

functions.name: mpg123_set_substring
functions.signature: EXPORT int mpg123_set_substring(mpg123_string *sb, const char *stuff, size_t from, size_t count);
functions.description: Replaces the contents of an mpg123_string with a substring [from, from+count) from a C-string and appends a null byte.
requirements: sb must be a valid mpg123_string.
stuff must point to a valid character buffer with at least from+count bytes accessible.

functions.name: mpg123_enc_from_id3
functions.signature: EXPORT enum mpg123_text_encoding mpg123_enc_from_id3(unsigned char id3_enc_byte);
functions.description: Converts an ID3v2 encoding byte to an mpg123_text_encoding value.

import io
import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid MPEG audio byte streams suitable for libmpg123 inputs.
# It can emit:
# - Minimal valid MP3 frames (Layer III) with common sample rates/bitrates
# - CBR/VBR mixtures
# - Optional ID3v2 tag at start
# - Optional ID3v1 tag at end
# - Optional ICY metadata block (Shoutcast) style
# The result is a bytes object <= 4096 bytes, deterministic per seed but varied.

# Tables based on MPEG1 Layer III common parameters
BITRATES_KBPS_MPEG1_L3 = [None, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256, 320, None]
SAMPLE_RATES_HZ_MPEG1 = [44100, 48000, 32000, None]
CHANNEL_MODE = [0, 1, 2, 3]  # stereo, joint-stereo, dual, mono

# For MPEG Version 2 (0b10) / 2.5 (0b00) Layer III
BITRATES_KBPS_MPEG2_L3 = [None, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 144, 160, None]
SAMPLE_RATES_HZ_MPEG2 = [22050, 24000, 16000, None]
SAMPLE_RATES_HZ_MPEG25 = [11025, 12000, 8000, None]

# Side info sizes for Layer III
# MPEG1: 32 bytes for mono, 17 for mono? Actually: MPEG1 L3: 32 bytes stereo, 17 bytes mono
# MPEG2/2.5: 17 bytes stereo, 9 bytes mono

def _frame_header(version_id: int, layer: int, protection_absent: int,
                  bitrate_idx: int, sampling_idx: int, padding: int,
                  private_bit: int, channel_mode: int, mode_ext: int,
                  copyright_bit: int, original: int, emphasis: int) -> bytes:
    # Assemble 32-bit header
    # AAAAAAAA AAABBCCD EEEEFFGH IIJJKLMM
    # We'll build fields per spec
    sync = 0x7FF
    header = 0
    header |= (sync << 21)
    header |= ((version_id & 0x3) << 19)
    header |= ((layer & 0x3) << 17)
    header |= ((protection_absent & 0x1) << 16)
    header |= ((bitrate_idx & 0xF) << 12)
    header |= ((sampling_idx & 0x3) << 10)
    header |= ((padding & 0x1) << 9)
    header |= ((private_bit & 0x1) << 8)
    header |= ((channel_mode & 0x3) << 6)
    header |= ((mode_ext & 0x3) << 4)
    header |= ((copyright_bit & 0x1) << 3)
    header |= ((original & 0x1) << 2)
    header |= ((emphasis & 0x3) << 0)
    return struct.pack('>I', header)


def _pick_version_and_tables(rng: random.Random):
    # version_id: 3=MPEG1, 2=MPEG2, 0=MPEG2.5; 1 is reserved
    vid_choice = rng.choice([3, 2, 0])
    if vid_choice == 3:
        bitrates = BITRATES_KBPS_MPEG1_L3
        srs = SAMPLE_RATES_HZ_MPEG1
        ver_mul = 144  # coefficient for frame length
        sideinfo_stereo = 32
        sideinfo_mono = 17
    elif vid_choice == 2:
        bitrates = BITRATES_KBPS_MPEG2_L3
        srs = SAMPLE_RATES_HZ_MPEG2
        ver_mul = 72
        sideinfo_stereo = 17
        sideinfo_mono = 9
    else:
        bitrates = BITRATES_KBPS_MPEG2_L3
        srs = SAMPLE_RATES_HZ_MPEG25
        ver_mul = 72
        sideinfo_stereo = 17
        sideinfo_mono = 9
    return vid_choice, bitrates, srs, ver_mul, sideinfo_stereo, sideinfo_mono


def _frame_length_bytes(ver_mul: int, bitrate_kbps: int, sr_hz: int, padding: int) -> int:
    # Layer III: frame_length = floor(ver_mul * bitrate / sample_rate) + padding, where bitrate in kbps -> bps
    # But ver_mul uses bytes: (144000 * kbps) / sr for MPEG1; (72000 * kbps) / sr for others
    # Our ver_mul is already 144 or 72 representing 144000/1000
    return int((ver_mul * 1000 * bitrate_kbps) // sr_hz) + padding


def _make_mp3_frame(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    version_id, bitrates_tbl, srs_tbl, ver_mul, sideinfo_stereo, sideinfo_mono = _pick_version_and_tables(rng)
    layer = 0b01  # Layer III
    protection_absent = 1  # no CRC for simplicity

    # pick valid indices
    # Ensure non-None bitrate and sample rate
    while True:
        br_idx = rng.randrange(1, 15)
        if bitrates_tbl[br_idx] is not None:
            break
    while True:
        sr_idx = rng.randrange(0, 3)
        if srs_tbl[sr_idx] is not None:
            break

    padding = rng.randrange(0, 2)
    private_bit = rng.randrange(0, 2)
    channel_mode = rng.choice(CHANNEL_MODE)
    mode_ext = rng.randrange(0, 4) if channel_mode == 1 else 0
    copyright_bit = rng.randrange(0, 2)
    original = rng.randrange(0, 2)
    emphasis = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])  # avoid reserved 3

    header = _frame_header(version_id, layer, protection_absent, br_idx, sr_idx,
                           padding, private_bit, channel_mode, mode_ext,
                           copyright_bit, original, emphasis)

    bitrate_kbps = bitrates_tbl[br_idx]
    sr_hz = srs_tbl[sr_idx]
    frame_len = _frame_length_bytes(144 if version_id == 3 else 72, bitrate_kbps, sr_hz, padding)

    # Side info size to keep internals plausible
    sideinfo_size = sideinfo_mono if channel_mode == 3 else sideinfo_stereo

    # Layer III has 4 bytes header + sideinfo + main_data (huffman) + (optional) ancillary
    # We'll synthesize main_data with zeros; decoders typically handle it as silence or error-resilient content.
    remaining = max(frame_len - 4, 0)
    sideinfo = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(min(sideinfo_size, remaining)))
    rest = remaining - len(sideinfo)
    if rest < 0:
        rest = 0
    # Fill Huffman and ancillary with zeros; include some non-zero for variability
    main_and_anc = bytearray(rest)
    for i in range(min(8, rest)):
        main_and_anc[i] = rng.randrange(0, 256)

    return header + sideinfo + bytes(main_and_anc)


def _make_id3v2_tag(rng: random.Random, max_size: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a compact ID3v2.3 tag with TIT2 and TPE1 frames in UTF-8
    if max_size < 32:
        return b""
    version = 3
    flags = 0

    frames = []
    def synchsafe(n: int) -> bytes:
        # 28-bit synchsafe
        b0 = (n >> 21) & 0x7F
        b1 = (n >> 14) & 0x7F
        b2 = (n >> 7) & 0x7F
        b3 = n & 0x7F
        return bytes([b0, b1, b2, b3])

    def make_text_frame(fid: bytes, text: str) -> bytes:
        enc = b"\x03"  # UTF-8
        payload = enc + text.encode('utf-8')
        size = len(payload)
        return fid + struct.pack('>I', size) + b"\x00\x00" + payload

    title = "Fuzz Song %d" % rng.randrange(0, 100000)
    artist = "Artist %d" % rng.randrange(0, 100000)
    frames.append(make_text_frame(b"TIT2", title))
    frames.append(make_text_frame(b"TPE1", artist))
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        album = "Album %d" % rng.randrange(0, 100000)
        frames.append(make_text_frame(b"TALB", album))

    body = b"".join(frames)
    total_size = len(body)
    header = b"ID3" + bytes([version, 0]) + bytes([flags]) + synchsafe(total_size)
    tag = header + body
    if len(tag) > max_size:
        return b""
    return tag


def _make_id3v1_tag(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 128-byte ID3v1 tag
    tag = bytearray(128)
    tag[0:3] = b"TAG"
    def put_str(off: int, size: int, s: str):
        b = s.encode('latin-1', 'ignore')[:size]
        tag[off:off+size] = b + b"\x00" * (size - len(b))
    put_str(3, 30, "Fuzz Title %d" % rng.randrange(100000))
    put_str(33, 30, "Fuzz Artist %d" % rng.randrange(100000))
    put_str(63, 30, "Fuzz Album %d" % rng.randrange(100000))
    put_str(93, 4, str(1980 + rng.randrange(50)))
    put_str(97, 30, "Comment")
    tag[127] = rng.randrange(0, 255)
    return bytes(tag)


def _make_icy_block(rng: random.Random, interval: int) -> bytes:
    # Shoutcast-style: after 'interval' bytes of audio, a metadata block appears:
    # 1 byte length = n (actual bytes = n*16), followed by that many bytes, padded to multiple of 16.
    # We'll make a small block like "StreamTitle='X';"
    title = "StreamTitle='Fuzz %d';" % rng.randrange(100000)
    meta = title.encode('latin-1')
    # pad to multiple of 16
    pad_len = (16 - (len(meta) % 16)) % 16
    block = meta + (b"\x00" * pad_len)
    n = len(block) // 16
    return bytes([n]) + block


def _assemble_stream(rng: random.Random, target_size: int) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = target_size

    # Optional ID3v2 at start
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        tag = _make_id3v2_tag(rng, min(512, remaining))
        parts.append(tag)
        remaining -= len(tag)

    # Build a sequence of frames, optionally inserting ICY blocks
    frames: List[bytes] = []
    icy = rng.random() < 0.25
    icy_interval = rng.choice([16000, 8192, 4096]) if icy else None
    bytes_since_meta = 0

    while remaining > 256 and len(frames) < 100:
        frame = _make_mp3_frame(rng)
        if len(frame) == 0 or len(frame) > remaining:
            break
        frames.append(frame)
        remaining -= len(frame)
        if icy:
            bytes_since_meta += len(frame)
            if bytes_since_meta >= icy_interval and remaining > 32:
                block = _make_icy_block(rng, icy_interval)
                if len(block) < remaining:
                    frames.append(block)
                    remaining -= len(block)
                    bytes_since_meta = 0

    parts.extend(frames)

    # Optional ID3v1 at end if space allows
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and remaining >= 128:
        v1 = _make_id3v1_tag(rng)
        parts.append(v1)
        remaining -= len(v1)

    # If we still have room, append a few more frames or padding
    while remaining > 0:
        f = _make_mp3_frame(rng)
        if len(f) == 0 or len(f) > remaining:
            # pad with zeros (ancillary data / trailing bytes)
            parts.append(b"\x00" * min(remaining, 64))
            remaining -= min(remaining, 64)
        else:
            parts.append(f)
            remaining -= len(f)
        if remaining < 64:
            break

    return b"".join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a target size up to 4096
    size = rng.randrange(512, 4096)
    # Bias sometimes smaller for feed mode tests
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        size = rng.randrange(64, 1024)

    data = _assemble_stream(rng, size)

    # Ensure non-empty and within limit
    if not data:
        data = _make_mp3_frame(rng)
    return data[:4096]

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target: Generate bytes for FUZZ_PARAM_STR used to seed mpg123_string copying.
# The fuzzer stub copies a substring of FUZZ_PARAM_STR into an mpg123_string,
# taking at most (len(src) % 64) bytes and appending a NUL. It may include NULs.
# Our goal: produce interesting yet valid arbitrary binary strings covering:
# - ASCII text of varying lengths
# - UTF-8 multibyte sequences
# - Embedded NULs and control chars
# - Repeated patterns, increasing size up to <64 effective bytes used
# - Edge cases around boundaries: 0, 1, 63, 64, 65 (mod 64 behavior)
# - Mixed bytes across full 0..255 range
# Note: The stub only copies up to 63 bytes due to modulo, but full src length
# still influences take = len(src) % 64, so we tailor lengths to exercise
# different remainders.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_bytes(rnd: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _utf8_samples() -> List[bytes]:
    # Valid UTF-8 sequences of various widths
    samples = [
        b"",  # empty
        b"A",  # single ASCII
        "Hello, mpg123!".encode("utf-8"),
        "\u00A9\u20AC".encode("utf-8"),            # ©€
        "\u03B1\u03B2\u03B3".encode("utf-8"),      # αβγ
        "\U0001F3B5\U0001F3A7".encode("utf-8"),    # 🎵🎧
        ("x" * 70).encode("utf-8"),                 # >64 length
    ]
    return samples

def _control_mix(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix printable, control, and NUL
    parts = [b"ID3", b"\x00", b"\x01\x02\x03", b"\n\r\t", b"END"]
    rnd.shuffle(parts)
    return b"".join(parts)

def _boundary_lengths() -> List[int]:
    # Choose lengths to yield diverse len % 64 values
    return [0, 1, 2, 15, 31, 32, 33, 62, 63, 64, 65, 95, 126, 127, 128, 129]

def _pattern_block(byte: int, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([byte]) * n

def _assemble_pool(rnd: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    pool: List[bytes] = []

    # UTF-8 samples
    pool.extend(_utf8_samples())

    # Boundary-sized ASCII blocks
    for n in _boundary_lengths():
        pool.append(b"A" * n)

    # Full 0..255 ramp truncated to various sizes (exercise arbitrary binary)
    ramp = bytes(range(256))
    for n in [7, 13, 31, 47, 63, 64, 80, 127, 255]:
        pool.append(ramp[:n])

    # Embedded NULs at different positions
    for n in [0, 1, 5, 10, 63, 70]:
        s = b"pre" + b"\x00" + _rand_bytes(rnd, n) + b"\x00" + b"post"
        pool.append(s)

    # Repeated patterns
    for bval in [0x00, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA]:
        for n in [3, 8, 16, 33, 63, 96]:
            pool.append(_pattern_block(bval, n))

    # Control mix randomizations
    for _ in range(6):
        pool.append(_control_mix(rnd))

    # Random length chunks with constrained max to keep result <= 4096
    for _ in range(10):
        n = rnd.randint(0, 256)
        pool.append(_rand_bytes(rnd, n))

    # Compose some concatenations to influence len%64 and content diversity
    concat_candidates = [
        b"TAG" + b"\x00" + b"\xff\xfe" + b"data" * 10,
        (b"\x01\x02\x03\x04" * 20) + b"trail",
        ("META:".encode() + "🎶".encode("utf-8") * 10),
    ]
    pool.extend(concat_candidates)

    # Ensure several lengths that map to each remainder 0..63
    # by generating small strings of exact sizes 0..127 to hit all remainders twice
    for size in range(0, 128):
        pool.append(bytes((size % 256,)) * size)

    return pool

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    pool = _assemble_pool(rnd)

    # Choose 1..4 entries and join with occasional NUL separator to add embedded NULs
    count = rnd.randint(1, 4)
    chosen = rnd.sample(pool, k=count)

    # Randomly interleave separators
    out = bytearray()
    for i, chunk in enumerate(chosen):
        out.extend(chunk)
        if i + 1 < count and rnd.random() < 0.6:
            # Insert a separator chosen from a set, including NUL
            sep_choice = rnd.choice([b"\x00", b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\xff\x00", b"--"])
            out.extend(sep_choice)

    # Trim to MAX_TOTAL
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        del out[MAX_TOTAL:]

    return bytes(out)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: arbitrary binary as a C-string (bytes terminated by a single NUL when consumed).
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to provide C-strings for:
#  - mpg123_add_string(sb, cstr)
#  - mpg123_add_substring(sb, cstr, from, count)
#  - mpg123_set_string(sb, cstr)
#  - mpg123_set_substring(sb, cstr, from, count)
# And a constructor stub that seeds a mpg123_string using FUZZ_PARAM_STR().
#
# Our goal is to generate a single bytes buffer that the harness splits (or reuses) for FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# We thus pack multiple interesting C-strings into one buffer, separated by NUL bytes, so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# can take a slice up to the next NUL and remain valid. Each segment is designed to exercise different behaviors:
#  - ASCII printable text of varied lengths
#  - UTF-8 multibyte sequences (emojis, non-Latin scripts)
#  - Latin-1/CP1252-like bytes (0x80..0xFF)
#  - Embedded NULs are not useful inside one C-string (would truncate), so we avoid interior NULs
#  - Repetitive patterns and alternating patterns for substring ranges
#  - Very short and relatively longer strings (but keep total <= 4096 bytes)
#  - Whitespace, control characters (except NUL), and punctuation
#  - Edge cases: empty string, single char, power-of-two lengths
#
# The harness may call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times; by concatenating many NUL-terminated strings,
# it can sequentially consume them. Even if it reuses the first, it remains valid.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Printable ASCII plus some whitespace and punctuation
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " \t\r\n"
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    return s.encode('ascii', 'strict')

def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a string with a mix of code points that encode to multibyte sequences
    pools = [
        (0x00A0, 0x024F),   # Latin extended
        (0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
        (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
        (0x0590, 0x05FF),   # Hebrew
        (0x0600, 0x06FF),   # Arabic
        (0x0900, 0x097F),   # Devanagari
        (0x3040, 0x309F),   # Hiragana
        (0x30A0, 0x30FF),   # Katakana
        (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),   # CJK Unified Ideographs
        (0x1F300, 0x1F6FF), # Emojis and symbols
    ]
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    out = []
    for _ in range(length):
        r = rng.random()
        if r < 0.2:
            # include some ASCII as well
            out.append(chr(rng.randint(0x21, 0x7E)))
        else:
            lo, hi = rng.choice(pools)
            out.append(chr(rng.randint(lo, hi)))
    s = ''.join(out)
    # Ensure it encodes; if not, fallback to replacement strategy by retrying limited times
    for _ in range(3):
        try:
            return s.encode('utf-8')
        except UnicodeEncodeError:
            # mutate one character
            i = rng.randrange(len(s))
            s = s[:i] + 'A' + s[i+1:]
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')

def _rand_latin1_bytes(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Choose bytes from 0x20..0xFF excluding 0x00; include control chars except NUL occasionally
    bs = bytearray()
    for _ in range(length):
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            b = rng.choice([0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D, 0x1B])
        else:
            b = rng.randint(0x20, 0xFF)
        if b == 0:
            b = 0x20
        bs.append(b)
    return bytes(bs)

def _pattern(rng: random.Random, token: bytes, min_reps: int, max_reps: int) -> bytes:
    reps = rng.randint(min_reps, max_reps)
    return token * reps

def _power_of_two_len(rng: random.Random, base: int = 1, max_power: int = 10) -> bytes:
    # Create a string whose length is a power of two
    power = rng.randint(base, max_power)
    length = 1 << power
    # Build using alternating characters
    a = rng.choice(b"AaBbCcDdEe")
    b = rng.choice(b"XxYyZz")
    return (bytes([a, b]) * (length // 2))[:length]

def _no_nul(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure there is no interior NUL to avoid premature termination for C-strings
    if b"\x00" not in data:
        return data
    return data.replace(b"\x00", b" ")

def _build_segments(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    segs: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Empty string edge case
    segs.append(b"")

    # 2) Tiny strings
    segs.append(_no_nul(b"A"))
    segs.append(_no_nul(b"0"))
    segs.append(_no_nul(b"\t"))

    # 3) Printable ASCII random
    segs.append(_no_nul(_rand_ascii(rng, 5, 32)))
    segs.append(_no_nul(_rand_ascii(rng, 33, 64)))

    # 4) UTF-8 variety
    segs.append(_no_nul(_rand_utf8(rng, 4, 24)))
    segs.append(_no_nul(_rand_utf8(rng, 16, 64)))

    # 5) Latin-1/CP1252-like
    segs.append(_no_nul(_rand_latin1_bytes(rng, 8, 40)))

    # 6) Repetitive patterns for substring behaviors
    segs.append(_no_nul(_pattern(rng, b"AB", 8, 64)))
    segs.append(_no_nul(_pattern(rng, b"xyz", 8, 48)))

    # 7) Alternating punctuation
    segs.append(_no_nul(_pattern(rng, b"-=_+[]{}()", 3, 8)))

    # 8) Power-of-two length strings (useful for buffer boundary conditions)
    segs.append(_no_nul(_power_of_two_len(rng, base=3, max_power=9)))

    # 9) Whitespace-heavy
    segs.append(_no_nul(b" " * rng.randint(1, 64) + b"\n\r\t" * rng.randint(1, 8)))

    # 10) Mixed digits and separators
    digits = ''.join(str((i % 10)) for i in range(rng.randint(16, 64)))
    segs.append(_no_nul((digits + ":" + digits[::-1]).encode('ascii')))

    # 11) Longish UTF-8 with emojis
    segs.append(_no_nul(("music ") .encode('utf-8') + _rand_utf8(rng, 8, 24)))

    # 12) Path-like strings (common substring patterns)
    path_parts = ["/usr", "/local", "/share", "/music", "/Artist", "/Album", "/Track01.mp3"]
    rng.shuffle(path_parts)
    segs.append(_no_nul(''.join(path_parts).encode('utf-8')))

    # 13) ID3-like text labels
    labels = ["TIT2:Title", "TALB:Album", "TPE1:Artist", "COMM:Comment", "TCON:Genre"]
    rng.shuffle(labels)
    segs.append(_no_nul('|'.join(labels).encode('ascii')))

    # 14) Hex dump-like string
    hexchars = ''.join(rng.choice('0123456789ABCDEF') for _ in range(rng.randint(32, 128)))
    segs.append(_no_nul(hexchars.encode('ascii')))

    # 15) JSON-like snippet (punctuation-heavy)
    json_like = '{"key": "value", "n": %d, "arr": [1,2,3]}' % rng.randint(0, 100000)
    segs.append(_no_nul(json_like.encode('utf-8')))

    return segs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    segments = _build_segments(rng)

    # Randomly add a few extra segments to increase diversity per call
    extra_count = rng.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(extra_count):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.3:
            segments.append(_no_nul(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 48)))
        elif choice < 0.6:
            segments.append(_no_nul(_rand_utf8(rng, 4, 20)))
        else:
            segments.append(_no_nul(_rand_latin1_bytes(rng, 4, 32)))

    # Assemble: each segment is a separate C-string, so terminate with NUL between them.
    out = bytearray()
    for seg in segments:
        # Ensure room for seg + NUL and cap total size
        if len(out) + len(seg) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += seg
        out += b"\x00"

    # Guarantee at least one NUL-terminated string even in degenerate case
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(b"\x00")

    return bytes(out)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for ICY metadata strings suitable for mpg123_icy2utf8()
# - Must be a valid C-string (NUL-terminated when passed via std::string.c_str()).
# - Typical encodings: UTF-8 or Windows-1252 (CP-1252).
# - Typical structure: key=value pairs, especially StreamTitle='...';StreamUrl='...';
# - We provide a variety of plausible values, including edge cases like empty fields,
#   long titles, different quote styles, special chars, multi-byte UTF-8, and mixed content.

# Some CP-1252 bytes in range 0x80-0x9F map to printable characters in that codepage.
CP1252_BYTES = [
    0x80,  # Euro sign
    0x82, 0x83, 0x84, 0x85, 0x86, 0x87, 0x88, 0x89,
    0x8A, 0x8B, 0x8C, 0x8E,
    0x91, 0x92, 0x93, 0x94, 0x95, 0x96, 0x97, 0x98, 0x99,
    0x9A, 0x9B, 0x9C, 0x9E, 0x9F
]

UTF8_EMOJI = [
    "😀", "🎵", "🎶", "🔥", "❤️", "😊", "🥁", "🎸", "🎧", "📻"
]

UTF8_NON_LATIN = [
    "Музика",  # Cyrillic
    "音乐",     # Chinese
    "موسيقى",  # Arabic
    "楽曲",     # Japanese
    "음악",     # Korean
]

URLS = [
    "http://example.com", "https://station.example/stream",
    "https://t.co/abcdef", "http://localhost/",
    "https://music.example.com/artist/track"
]

ARTISTS = [
    "Unknown Artist", "Daft Punk", "Björk", "Sigur Rós", "AC/DC",
    "Guns N' Roses", "René LaTaupe", "Lady Gaga", "Metallica",
    "Aphex Twin", "Adele", "王菲", "محمد منير"
]

TITLES = [
    "Live Mix", "Best Of 90s", "Summer Hits", "Ambient Session",
    "Café del Mar", "Été Indien", "Für Elise", "¡Viva la Vida!",
    "Гимн радости", "夜曲 No.2", "مرحبا", "사랑의 노래"
]

GENRES = [
    "Pop", "Rock", "EDM", "Classical", "Jazz", "Talk", "News",
    "Chillout", "Ambient", "Hip-Hop", "World"
]

QUOTES = ["'", '"']


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Use printable ASCII without control chars or semicolons/equals to avoid breaking ICY fields unless desired
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_./,()[]{}:+&@#"
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_cp1252_bytes(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    b = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            # Mostly regular Latin-1 printable
            b.append(r.randint(0x20, 0x7E))
        else:
            b.append(r.choice(CP1252_BYTES))
    return bytes(b)


def _utf8_mix(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Compose a mixture of ASCII, emoji, and non-latin words
    parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 3, 12))
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        parts.append(r.choice(UTF8_EMOJI))
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(r.choice(UTF8_NON_LATIN))
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 3, 12))
    return ' '.join(parts)


def _make_stream_title(r: random.Random, quote: str) -> str:
    # Generate plausible StreamTitle value
    artist = r.choice(ARTISTS)
    title = r.choice(TITLES)
    sep = " - " if r.random() < 0.8 else " – "
    extra = ""
    # Optionally add featuring, remix, emoji, or year
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        extra = f" (feat. {_rand_ascii(r, 3, 10)})"
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        extra += " [Remix]"
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        extra += " " + r.choice(UTF8_EMOJI)
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        extra += f" ({r.randint(1980, 2025)})"
    core = f"{artist}{sep}{title}{extra}"
    # Occasionally produce a long title
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        core += " - " + _utf8_mix(r)
    return f"StreamTitle={quote}{core}{quote};"


def _make_stream_url(r: random.Random, quote: str) -> str:
    url = r.choice(URLS)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        # add query params
        q = {
            "utm_source": "radio",
            "id": str(r.randint(1, 999999)),
            "genre": r.choice(GENRES).lower()
        }
        url = f"{url}?utm_source={q['utm_source']}&id={q['id']}&genre={q['genre']}"
    return f"StreamUrl={quote}{url}{quote};"


def _make_kv_extra(r: random.Random, quote: str) -> str:
    keys = ["Genre", "Bitrate", "Listeners", "DJ", "StationName", "StationDescription"]
    k = r.choice(keys)
    if k == "Bitrate":
        v = str(r.choice([64, 96, 128, 192, 256, 320]))
    elif k == "Listeners":
        v = str(r.randint(0, 5000))
    elif k in ("StationName", "StationDescription"):
        v = _utf8_mix(r)
    elif k == "Genre":
        v = r.choice(GENRES)
    else:
        v = r.choice(ARTISTS)
    return f"{k}={quote}{v}{quote};"


def _icy_block_utf8(r: random.Random) -> str:
    quote = r.choice(QUOTES)
    parts = []
    # Common fields
    parts.append(_make_stream_title(r, quote))
    if r.random() < 0.9:
        parts.append(_make_stream_url(r, quote))
    # Optional extras
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)):
        parts.append(_make_kv_extra(r, quote))
    # Sometimes include simple key without quotes
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(f"Bitrate={r.choice([64,96,128,192,256,320])};")
    return ''.join(parts)


def _icy_block_cp1252(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build ICY fields but values are encoded as CP-1252 bytes
    quote = r.choice(QUOTES)
    # ASCII key part
    def enc(v: str) -> bytes:
        # attempt encoding to cp1252, fallback: replace with similar ASCII
        return v.encode('cp1252', errors='replace')
    parts = []
    artist = r.choice(ARTISTS)
    title = r.choice(TITLES)
    sep = " - "
    core = f"StreamTitle={quote}{artist}{sep}{title}{quote};"
    parts.append(core.encode('ascii', errors='ignore'))
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        url = _make_stream_url(r, quote)
        parts.append(url.encode('ascii', errors='ignore'))
    # Add some raw cp1252 bytes into description-like field
    raw = _rand_cp1252_bytes(r, 5, 20)
    extra = f"StationDescription={quote}".encode('ascii') + raw + quote.encode('ascii') + b";"
    parts.append(extra)
    return b''.join(parts)


def _choose_variant(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return r.choice([
        "utf8_basic",           # Standard UTF-8, typical fields
        "utf8_long",            # Long title and extras
        "utf8_minimal",         # Only StreamTitle
        "utf8_empty_fields",    # Empty or missing values
        "cp1252_basic",         # CP-1252 encoded bytes
        "utf8_mixed_quotes",    # Use different quotes across fields
    ])


def _build_utf8_minimal(r: random.Random) -> str:
    quote = r.choice(QUOTES)
    value = r.choice(ARTISTS) + " - " + r.choice(TITLES)
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        value = ""
    return f"StreamTitle={quote}{value}{quote};"


def _build_utf8_long(r: random.Random) -> str:
    quote = r.choice(QUOTES)
    s = _icy_block_utf8(r)
    # Inflate with additional k=v; pairs
    extra_pairs = r.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(extra_pairs):
        s += _make_kv_extra(r, quote)
    # Append a large, but still reasonable, UTF-8 title tail
    long_tail = ' ' + ' '.join(_utf8_mix(r) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)))
    s += f"LongNote={quote}{long_tail}{quote};"
    return s


def _build_utf8_mixed_quotes(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Alternate quotes to exercise parser
    parts = []
    parts.append(_make_stream_title(r, '"'))
    parts.append(_make_stream_url(r, '\''))
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        q = '"' if r.random() < 0.5 else '\''
        parts.append(_make_kv_extra(r, q))
    return ''.join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    variant = _choose_variant(r)

    if variant == "cp1252_basic":
        data = _icy_block_cp1252(r)
        # Ensure size limit
        if len(data) > 4096:
            data = data[:4096]
        return data

    if variant == "utf8_minimal":
        s = _build_utf8_minimal(r)
    elif variant == "utf8_long":
        s = _build_utf8_long(r)
    elif variant == "utf8_mixed_quotes":
        s = _build_utf8_mixed_quotes(r)
    elif variant == "utf8_empty_fields":
        q = r.choice(QUOTES)
        s = f"StreamTitle={q}{q};StreamUrl={q}{q};"
    else:  # utf8_basic
        s = _icy_block_utf8(r)

    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b
